spec.title: Fast Rust compiler: workstation setup and ownership

p.SCOPE: A normal flow installs portable work rules and OS-gated Linux agent instructions. Its skills execute only in response to an explicit owner setup/removal command. There are no lifecycle script handlers, binaries, privileged services or automatic package install/uninstall hooks.

p.PORTABILITY: Local acceleration must not make a repository require a machine path, linker, experimental compiler or filesystem. Keep repository Cargo configuration portable and its toolchain stable; local overrides/configuration live outside tracked source. Setup verifies any existing repository-local accelerator keys and proposes removal within the authorized project scope, preserving aliases and unrelated settings.

p.PARAMETERS: Select workspace root, project root, warm source, Cargo install root, state home, nightly channel, target triple, compiler thread count and build parallelism from actual local observations and owner intent. No product checkout name or absolute machine root is a shipped default. Recommended baseline is stable plus LLVM, clang/mold, sccache and nextest on a supported GNU/Linux host; nightly/Cranelift is an explicit optional profile.

p.CONFIG-HIERARCHY: Inventory home, ancestor, project and extensionless Cargo configs and relevant environment overrides before edits. Prefer a selected untracked ancestor configuration over global settings. Preserve TOML structure, unknown keys and comments. Scalar/profile settings and rustflags arrays have different Cargo merge behavior; do not duplicate linker/thread flags across levels. A closer repository toolchain can override a parent rustup selection: verify the effective toolchain in the project and every new worktree.

p.PREPARE-BEFORE-APPLY: Before machine writes persist a local plan and ownership baseline. An explicit setup command authorizes its concrete in-scope steps; it does not authorize repartitioning, formatting disks, global toolchain defaults, deleting caches/worktrees or changing unrelated projects. Package-manager privilege failures stop that step with exact pending instructions. Never hide failure or retry effects with unknown outcomes.

p.LOCAL-RECEIPTS: Use a uniquely named directory under the selected user state home, default `~/.vibe/fast-rust-compiler/`, with private permissions. Record prior tool versions/presence, exact override paths/channels, original values/absence of modified configuration keys, selected profiles and commands/exit codes/verification. Update after each step. Never copy credential values into plans/reports. Back up only safe configuration content; credential-bearing files require scoped value restoration without copying secrets.

p.PRESERVE-OWNERSHIP: Existing tools, overrides and settings are adopted observations, not newly owned installations. Rerunning setup reuses the existing receipt and applies only missing or explicitly changed steps. Record partial setup before stopping. If no receipt predates an existing configuration, never invent a before-state or claim ownership.

p.MEASURE: Use affected nonzero checks and a disposable representative fixture to verify compiler/linker/tool availability and cold/warm behavior. Report timings, source/tool versions and cache hit/miss/noncacheable counters; neither the name fast nor the presence of a cache proves speed. Keep workspace incremental compilation unless measured evidence justifies changing it. Optimized dependency/build-script profiles trade initial compile cost for repeated runtime benefit.

p.FILESYSTEM-AWARE-SETUP: Inventory source and destination filesystem types, mount boundaries and free space before selecting a warm-target strategy. XFS with working reflink supports a cheap initial copy-on-write file clone, not zero-cost metadata or future writes; later builds can allocate additional space. An XFS name alone does not prove reflink is enabled or cross-mount cloning works. Verify a tiny real clone on the selected filesystem. Ordinary ext4 must not be assumed to support this operation; skip cloning after an unsupported probe. Windows, including NTFS hosts, skips this recipe. Other Unix filesystems use observed clone support rather than a name whitelist. Never reformat, remount, change filesystem features or replace a failed clone with an ordinary full target copy during setup.

p.EXPERIMENTAL-LIMIT: Cranelift is optional, target/component availability and compiler features vary by nightly. On backend/SIMD/assembly/panic compatibility failure report the failing crate and actual error. Do not silently switch compiler settings or weaken tests. A user-selected LLVM profile provides a deliberate escape path. Optional compiler threads are tunable, not an unconditional fixed machine-wide value.

p.UNDO: Removal first restores recorded settings and overrides, then removes only newly installed tools not needed elsewhere. Check current values against recorded applied values; preserve unrelated later edits and surface conflicting drift before removal. Remove wrappers/config references before removing their tools. Keep shared installations, user caches, source and worktrees; no `apt autoremove`, blanket Cargo cache deletion or rustup self uninstall. Restore prior directory overrides individually rather than assuming no prior override.

p.BOOT-INDEPENDENT-OF-MACHINE: The portable boot is unconditional; the Linux setup fragment declares `when = "os:linux"`. Dynamic boot loading reads files only. Machine provisioning is a separately user-commanded agent action, even after the flow has been installed.

p.GUIDES: Operator recipes: package-relative `docs/setup.md`, `docs/remove.md`; reusable templates: `templates/cargo-home.toml`, `templates/linux-llvm.toml`, `templates/linux-cranelift.toml`. They are input examples for reviewed local edits, never auto-copied into a repository.
